cases.title: Power-up connection reset state

requirements.text: The Device shall execute a connection reset after power-up.
Connection reset: activate master only; extension connections not activated.
Connection reset: MasterHostConnectionID = 0x00000000.
Connection reset: StreamPacketSizeMax = 0 (only IDLE sent on master).
Connection reset: stream control reset — packet tag restarts at 0; first packet on connection 0.
Connection reset: TestMode = 0, TestErrorCountSelector = 0, all test counters = 0.
Connection reset: HsUpconnection = 0/1 per support; Device trigger signal = 0; XmlManifestSelector = 0.
Connection reset shall initialise the master connection bit rate to the lowest discovery bit rate the Device supports, with the corresponding value in ConnectionConfig (1 connection).
Device shall de-assert its trigger signal as part of link discovery, equivalent to a falling-edge trigger packet.
XmlManifestSize ≥ 1; XmlManifestSelector holds 0..XmlManifestSize−1. ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Reaction to an out-of-range selector write not specified.

cases.objective: Verify that after power-up the Device is in the connection-reset state defined by §10.3.28.
cases.preconditions: DUT unpowered; exerciser connected to connection 0 (and all extensions if MULTI); no prior configuration.
equipment: CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
procedure: Apply power (in SIM: release all resets).
Observe the downconnection with the analyzer from the first character.
Sweep the exerciser receiver over the discovery rates (1.25, 3.125 Gbps) until Detected.

Over the master LS upconnection read: ConnectionConfig, MasterHostConnectionID, StreamPacketSizeMax, TestMode, TestErrorCountSelector, TestErrorCount/TestPacketCountTx/Rx for every selector, HsUpconnection, XmlManifestSelector, ConnectionReset.
Check extension connections carry no link activity (MULTI).
Check no trigger asserted inside the Device (probe/sim signal).
cases.stimulus: Power-on; read commands (Cmd 0x00, B = 4 or 8) to the listed bootstrap addresses.
cases.expected: Master transmits IDLE only at the lowest supported discovery rate; ConnectionConfig = (1 connection, speed code of that rate); MasterHostConnectionID = 0; StreamPacketSizeMax = 0; TestMode = 0; selector = 0; all counters = 0; XmlManifestSelector = 0; HsUpconnection = support bit; ConnectionReset = 0.
cases.pass_criteria: Every listed register equals its reset value; downconnection contains only IDLE words (no stream/test packets) until configured; extensions inactive.
cases.fail_criteria: Any register differs; any non-IDLE packet other than control acks; master at a non-discovery rate; extension active.
cases.evidence: Analyzer capture (first 10 ms), register dump log, sim transcript / waveform (FST).

emulator.scope: Power-up through the bench's power-on reset: §10.3.28 has the device execute a connection reset at power-up, so no ConnectionReset is written. Rate, extension and internal-trigger observations are outside the FIFO link. Needs the device's test bench (power-on reset); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Power-cycle the device through the bench (RESET, every input at 0) and wait for a quiet link.
Read ConnectionReset, MasterHostConnectionID, StreamPacketSizeMax, TestMode, TestErrorCountSelector, TestErrorCount, XmlManifestSelector (4 bytes) and TestPacketCountTx/Rx (8 bytes).
Read ConnectionConfig and HsUpconnection.
Record the downlink for 500 ms without sending commands.
Registers the check changes are restored afterwards.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every listed register reads 0; ConnectionConfig = 1 connection at discovery code 0x28 or 0x38; HsUpconnection bits 31:1 = 0; no stream or test packet in the 500 ms recording.
emulator.fail_criteria: Any register differs from its reset value; ConnectionConfig is not a discovery configuration; a stream or test packet arrives; a read is not acknowledged with 0x00.

cases.title: ConnectionReset via master: 200 ms, self-clear, rate fallback

requirements.text: On a ConnectionReset (write 0x00000001) received via the Master connection the Device shall execute connection reset and activate its discovery connection configuration within 200 ms.
The Device shall clear ConnectionReset back to 0x00000000 once the discovery configuration is active.
Connection reset shall initialise the master connection bit rate to the lowest discovery bit rate the Device supports, with the corresponding value in ConnectionConfig (1 connection).
Connection reset: stream control reset — packet tag restarts at 0; first packet on connection 0.

cases.objective: Verify ConnectionReset execution time, register self-clear and return to discovery configuration from an operational high-rate multi-connection state.
cases.preconditions: DUT discovered and running at its ConnectionConfigDefault; streaming active; StreamPacketSizeMax > 0.
equipment: CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
procedure: Start continuous acquisition and confirm stream packets on all connections.
Write 0x00000001 to 0x4000 via master (fire-and-forget; do not wait for ack).
Timestamp the write EOP (t0).
Re-lock the Host receiver at each discovery rate; record time t1 at which Detected is reached on master at the lowest supported discovery rate.
Read ConnectionReset, ConnectionConfig, StreamPacketSizeMax.
Repeat 100× with random write instants relative to stream packet boundaries.
cases.stimulus: Write command: Cmd 0x01, Size 0x000004, Addr 0x00004000, Data 0x00000001.
cases.expected: Device stops streaming, switches master to lowest discovery rate, disables extensions within 200 ms; ConnectionReset reads 0.
cases.pass_criteria: t(discovery config active) − t0 ≤ 200 ms in 100/100 trials; ConnectionReset = 0 on first successful read; ConnectionConfig = discovery value; SPSM = 0; no stream packet after reset.
cases.fail_criteria: Any trial > 200 ms; register not cleared; streaming continues; Device not detectable at a discovery rate.
cases.evidence: Analyzer timestamps table, per-trial CSV, register reads.

emulator.scope: 5 trials instead of 100; the rate fallback is judged by the ConnectionConfig value (no serial rate).
procedure: Program StreamPacketSizeMax if it is 0, start continuous acquisition, wait for an image header.
Wait 0..20 ms, write ConnectionReset = 1 without waiting for an ack (t0), wait 200 ms.
Read ConnectionReset, ConnectionConfig, StreamPacketSizeMax; keep recording for 300 ms.
Repeat 5 times.
Registers the check changes are restored afterwards.
emulator.pass_criteria: In every trial: ConnectionReset = 0, ConnectionConfig = discovery configuration, StreamPacketSizeMax = 0, and no stream packet arrives later than t0 + 200 ms.
emulator.fail_criteria: Register not cleared, ConnectionConfig not at discovery, SPSM not 0, streaming continues past 200 ms, or a read fails.

cases.title: ConnectionReset on extension connection is ignored

requirements.text: The Device shall ignore a connection reset received on an extension connection.
Extension connections provide read-only discovery access; DeviceConnectionID > 0 on extensions (may exceed 1).

cases.objective: Verify that a connection reset received on an extension connection is ignored.
cases.preconditions: MULTI Device, all connections discovered and streaming at ConnectionConfigDefault.
equipment: CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
procedure: Stream continuously.
Write 0x00000001 to ConnectionReset via extension connection k (each k ≥ 1).
Monitor all connections for 500 ms.
Read ConnectionConfig and packet tag continuity via master.
cases.stimulus: Write 0x00000001 to 0x4000 on extension connection k.
cases.expected: No reset: rate, connection count, streaming and packet tags continue uninterrupted.
cases.pass_criteria: No change in ConnectionConfig; no gap or restart in packet tags; master control channel still operational.

cases.title: Full discovery sequence against Host emulator

requirements.text: Device shall support at least one of the defined high speed bit rates (1.250/2.500/3.125/5.000/6.250 Gbps) in normal operation, plus a discovery rate (1.250 or 3.125 Gbps, per Table 1 discovery marks).
DeviceConnectionID shall return the ID of the Device connection through which it is read (0 = master).
MasterHostConnectionID shall hold the Host connection ID written via the master connection; 0x00000000 = unknown.
Device shall support control packets up to its maximum and report it in ControlPacketSizeMax: bytes, whole packet, multiple of 4, ≥ 128.
ConnectionConfigDefault shall provide the ConnectionConfig value of the Device's recommended mode.
Writing ConnectionConfig shall set the connection speed on the specified number of connections (used by the Host at discovery rate to enable extensions, §10.1.3).
HsUpconnection bit 0 = 1 if HS upconnection supported else 0; bits 31:1 = 0.
All mandatory bootstrap registers shall be implemented at the Table 45 addresses, lengths and access modes.

cases.objective: Run the complete §10.1 discovery flow and confirm every Device-side response.
cases.preconditions: DUT powered; exerciser implementing §10.1.2–10.1.6 host steps; control packet size limited to 128 bytes until CPSM read.
equipment: CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
procedure: Write ConnectionReset = 1 on every Host connection; wait 200 ms.
Lock at lowest discovery rate; if not Detected, try next discovery rate.
Read DeviceConnectionID via each detected connection.
Write MasterHostConnectionID (e.g. 0x00000001) via master; read back via every connection.
Read HsUpconnection; read ControlPacketSizeMax; write StreamPacketSizeMax (host max).
Read ConnectionConfigDefault; write ConnectionConfig with its connection count at discovery rate; verify extensions become Detected.
Write ConnectionConfig = ConnectionConfigDefault (operating rate) per §10.1.6.1; verify Detected on all connections.
Start acquisition; verify frames.
cases.stimulus: Host discovery command script (see sequence diagram).
cases.expected: Device detected at a discovery rate; DeviceConnectionID = physical connection index; MasterHostConnectionID readback identical on all connections; CPSM ≥ 128 and multiple of 4; operating mode reached.
cases.pass_criteria: All steps complete with success acks (0x00/0x01), link Detected at operating rate on all connections, first frame received error-free.
cases.fail_criteria: Any error ack, missing ack within 200 ms, Undetected connection after timeout, wrong ID values.
cases.evidence: Discovery log with each command/ack, analyzer capture, final register dump.

emulator.scope: The §10.1 Host order on one connection; rate locking steps collapse to register writes.
procedure: ConnectionReset, wait 200 ms.
Read DeviceConnectionID; write MasterHostConnectionID = 1 and read it back.
Read HsUpconnection and ControlPacketSizeMax; write StreamPacketSizeMax = the host maximum (--host-spsm) and read it back.
Read ConnectionConfigDefault; write it to ConnectionConfig and read it back.
Start acquisition through the XML and receive 1 image(s).
Registers the check changes are restored afterwards.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every command answered 0x00/0x01 within the plan's latency limit (--ack-latency); DeviceConnectionID = 0; read-backs equal the written values; ControlPacketSizeMax >= 128 and a multiple of 4; ConnectionConfigDefault has a Table 46 speed code; the first image is complete with no CRC error.
emulator.fail_criteria: Any error ack, missing ack or ack later than the plan's latency limit (--ack-latency), a wrong read-back or ID, or no complete image.

cases.title: Topology discovery with permuted cabling

requirements.text: DeviceConnectionID shall return the ID of the Device connection through which it is read (0 = master).
Extension connections provide read-only discovery access; DeviceConnectionID > 0 on extensions (may exceed 1).
The Device shall ignore a write to MasterHostConnectionID via an extension connection.
MasterHostConnectionID shall hold the Host connection ID written via the master connection; 0x00000000 = unknown.

cases.objective: Verify DeviceConnectionID / MasterHostConnectionID allow the Host to reconstruct any cable permutation (Figures 37–38).
cases.preconditions: MULTI Device; Host with ≥ n+1 connections; cable permutation table.
equipment: Reference CXP frame grabber (Host) with GenTL producer
CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
procedure: For each permutation of Device connections to Host ports (at least n cyclic shifts + one reversed):
Run discovery; read DeviceConnectionID on every Detected port.
Write a unique MasterHostConnectionID via the master; attempt a different value via an extension.
Read MasterHostConnectionID on every port.
cases.stimulus: Discovery per permutation; write via extension to 0x4008.
cases.expected: IDs match physical wiring; extension write ignored; all ports report the master's Host ID.
cases.pass_criteria: Topology reconstructed correctly for 100 % of permutations; extension write has no effect.
cases.fail_criteria: Wrong ID; extension write changes value; discovery fails for any permutation.
cases.evidence: Permutation matrix with read values, photos of cabling.

emulator.reason: The emulator link is a single connection, so extension-connection behaviour cannot be exercised. Topology permutations need several Host ports.

cases.title: Operating bit-rate change via ConnectionConfig

requirements.text: On a ConnectionConfig write that changes speed, the Device shall acknowledge at the original speed first, then switch all specified connections (and HS upconnection) to the new rate.
All connections forming one link, including an HS upconnection, shall operate at the same bit rate.

ConnectionConfig shall hold a valid (connections[31:16], speed code[15:0]) combination; speed codes 0x28/0x30/0x38/0x40/0x48. ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Error code for an invalid ConnectionConfig write (0x41 assumed) is not stated.
A ConnectionConfig write shall reset stream control (tag → 0, next packet on connection 0) even if the value is unchanged.

cases.objective: Verify ack-before-switch ordering and re-lock within 200 ms for every rate change.
cases.preconditions: Device discovered at discovery rate; list of valid ConnectionConfig values (from XML/documentation).
equipment: CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
procedure: For every ordered pair (from, to) of valid ConnectionConfig values:
Write ConnectionConfig = to; capture ack at old rate.
Switch Host receivers to the new rate; wait 200 ms; check Detected on all specified connections.
Read ConnectionConfig; start acquisition; confirm first packet tag = 0 on connection 0.
cases.stimulus: Write Cmd 0x01 to 0x4014 with value (connections << 16) | speed code.
cases.expected: Ack 0x01 received completely at the old rate before the rate changes; Device Detected at the new rate within 200 ms; tag restarts at 0.
cases.pass_criteria: 100 % of transitions: ack at old rate, Detected ≤ 200 ms + Host lock time, readback equals written value, first packet tag 0 on connection 0.
cases.fail_criteria: Ack missing/corrupted, switch before ack, lock failure, wrong readback, tag not reset.
cases.evidence: Transition matrix, analyzer captures around each switch.

emulator.reason: A bit-rate change has no meaning on the FIFO link (no serial rate, no receiver lock). ConnectionConfig register behaviour is covered by INIT-004, INIT-009 and the tag reset by DATA-003.

cases.title: StreamPacketSizeMax gating and limit

requirements.text: While StreamPacketSizeMax = 0 the Device shall not transmit stream packets.
Stream packet total size (first K27.7 to last K29.7) shall not exceed StreamPacketSizeMax (bytes).
The Device may use any packet size up to StreamPacketSizeMax (last packet of an image may be as small as 1 word).
Connection reset: StreamPacketSizeMax = 0 (only IDLE sent on master).

cases.objective: Verify no stream packets while SPSM = 0 and every stream packet ≤ SPSM bytes for each configured value.
equipment: FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
procedure: Write AcquisitionStart = 1 while SPSM = 0; observe 1 s.
For SPSM ∈ {36, 40, 128, 1024, 4096, 8192, host max}: write SPSM, stream ≥ 10 frames, measure every packet size (K27.7..K29.7).
Write SPSM = 0 again during streaming (behaviour record only).
cases.stimulus: Writes to 0x4010; AcquisitionStart via its bootstrap-provided address.
cases.expected: No stream packet while SPSM = 0; all packets ≤ SPSM; DsizeP ≤ (SPSM − 32)/4.
cases.pass_criteria: Zero violations over all packets and all SPSM values.
cases.fail_criteria: Any stream packet with SPSM = 0; any packet > SPSM.

emulator.scope: The largest SPSM tried is the host maximum (--host-spsm); the SPSM = 0 write during streaming is not repeated.

For each StreamPacketSizeMax of 36, 40, 128, 1024 and the host maximum (--host-spsm) bytes: write it, acquire 2000 stream packets, measure every stream packet from K27.7 to K29.7.
Registers the check changes are restored afterwards.

cases.title: High speed upconnection discovery and fallback

requirements.text: HS upconnection: when the Device reaches Detected (bit + word lock) on the HS upconnection it shall switch all upconnection communication to it.
HS upconnection: if the HS upconnection is disabled, or Undetected 200 ms after a speed change, the Device shall switch back to the low speed upconnection.
HsUpconnection bit 0 = 1 if HS upconnection supported else 0; bits 31:1 = 0.
If the HS upconnection loses lock and the Device cannot recover it, the Device shall switch back to the LS upconnection.
With HS upconnection in use, trigger ack timeout = 480 ns; Device decodes Table 16 triggers on the HS upconnection.

cases.objective: Verify §10.1.4 HS upconnection enable, switch-over and fallback behaviour.
cases.preconditions: HSUP Device with HS upconnection cable present; Host emulator supporting HS upconnection.
equipment: CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
procedure: Read HsUpconnection via LS; expect bit0 = 1.
Enable Host HS upconnection at downconnection rate sending IDLE; wait 200 ms.
Read HsUpconnection via HS upconnection; verify success.
Send commands/triggers on HS; verify responses.
Disable HS upconnection transmitter; verify Device resumes accepting commands on LS.
Change ConnectionConfig rate; keep HS upconnection off for > 200 ms; verify fallback to LS.
Break HS upconnection mid-transaction; verify recovery.
cases.stimulus: HS upconnection IDLE / commands / Table 16 triggers.
cases.expected: Device switches to HS when Detected, back to LS when HS disabled or undetected 200 ms after speed change.
cases.pass_criteria: All transitions succeed; no command lost after fallback beyond the one in flight.
cases.fail_criteria: Device stays on dead HS link; commands on LS ignored after fallback.
cases.evidence: Analyzer capture of both directions, command log.

emulator.reason: Needs a high-speed upconnection (HSUP); the FIFO link has one uplink and no bit rate.

Write it to ConnectionConfig and read ConnectionConfig back.

cases.title: 8B/10B code and running-disparity validity

requirements.text: Both upconnection and downconnection shall use 8B/10B coding.
Bit order: 8B/10B bit 'A' = LSB before coding; bit 'a' transmitted first.

cases.objective: Verify every transmitted 10-bit symbol is a valid 8B/10B code with correct running disparity, bit 'a' first.
cases.preconditions: Device streaming max-load images, then idle, then test mode.
equipment: CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
Python golden CXP codec (CRC-32, packet builder/parser, pixel packing model)
procedure: Capture ≥ 10⁹ characters per connection in each mode.
Decode with an independent 8B/10B decoder (IEEE tables incl. D.x.A7 rule).
Count code violations, disparity errors, comma occurrences outside P0 of IDLE (false commas).
In SIM: check the serializer bit order against Figure 15 using the IDLE word (BC 3C 3C B5 → 0011111010 …).
cases.expected: Zero code/disparity violations; commas (K28.5) only at IDLE P0; Figure 15 bit order.
cases.pass_criteria: 0 errors in ≥ 10⁹ chars per mode per connection.
cases.fail_criteria: Any invalid symbol, RD error, false comma in data.

emulator.reason: The FIFO link carries 32-bit words after 8B/10B decoding, without IDLE words or K-character flags, so 10-bit symbols and running disparity cannot be observed or injected.

cases.title: Word structure and K-code usage audit

requirements.text: K-codes shall be used only for the Table 11 functions (K27.7 SOP, K28.6 I/O ack, K28.1/K28.5 alignment, K28.2/K28.4 trigger, K28.3 stream marker, K29.7 EOP).
Transmission is in 4-character words P0..P3 sent P0 first (except 6-character LS trigger packets).
Device shall not send control commands; stream data only on the downconnection; control acks only in response to a received command.
Data packet: 4×K27.7, 4×type (0x01 stream, 0x02 cmd, 0x03 ack, 0x04 test), payload, 4×K29.7; other types reserved and not to be sent.

cases.objective: Verify every downconnection packet is word-aligned, uses only Table 11 K-codes for their functions, and uses only defined packet types and directions.
cases.preconditions: Captures from INIT-004, IMG-001, TRIG-001, PROT-010 runs.
equipment: CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
Python golden CXP codec (CRC-32, packet builder/parser, pixel packing model)
procedure: Parse all captures into words; check every packet start (K27.7 ×4, K28.6 ×4, K28.2/K28.4 ×4) begins at P0.
Check K27.7/K29.7 appear only as 4× start/end; K28.3 only as 4× stream marker inside stream packets; K28.1/K28.5 only in IDLE.
Check data packet type bytes ∈ {0x01, 0x03, 0x04} downstream; never 0x02 (command) from Device.
Check no K28.0 or other undefined K-codes.
cases.expected: Only defined K-code uses, packet types, directions.
cases.pass_criteria: Zero violations.
cases.fail_criteria: Any misaligned packet, undefined K-code, reserved/0x02 type from Device.

emulator.scope: Word-level audit of this session's own traffic (reads of Standard, Revision and DeviceVendorName, one write, 2 images): K-code positions inside words cannot be seen without K flags.
procedure: Record the downlink during those reads, the write and a 2-image acquisition.
Check every frame starts with 4xK27.7, ends with 4xK29.7 and has a 4x replicated type.
Check each type is 0x01, 0x03 or 0x04; count 0x02 and reserved types; note 0x05/0x06 host-stack extensions and SOP/EOP-valued words inside frame bodies.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every frame correctly framed; no type 0x02 or reserved type from the Device.
emulator.fail_criteria: A mis-framed packet, or a command/reserved type sent by the Device.

requirements.text: Idle time shall be filled with IDLE words K28.5 K28.1 K28.1 D21.5.

On a high speed connection an IDLE word shall be transmitted at least once every 100 words (all modes, incl. streaming and test packets). ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: A 1027-word connection test packet (§8.7.2) and long stream packets can only meet this by IDLE stretching (§8.2.5.2); the spec does not say so explicitly for test packets.
Packets on a high speed connection may be stretched with IDLE words; receivers should ignore them (not in CRC).

cases.objective: Verify IDLE words K28.5 K28.1 K28.1 D21.5 fill idle time and appear at least once every 100 words on every HS connection in every mode.

FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards

Compute the maximum run of non-IDLE words between IDLE words.
Verify IDLE words inside packets (stretching) are well-formed and packets remain parseable.

cases.title: Upconnection word alignment and re-alignment

requirements.text: The receiver shall perform word alignment.
IDLE presence should be checked on each active connection; after a threshold of misses the receiver should be reset (re-align).

cases.objective: Verify the Device LS receiver achieves and re-acquires word alignment from any bit/character phase.
cases.preconditions: SIM with bit-level LS channel model; exerciser with bit-slip injection on hardware.
equipment: FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
procedure: Start IDLE stream with each of 40 bit-phase offsets; measure time to aligned and first accepted command.
During operation inject 1, 2, 3 character slips and single bit slips; measure recovery.
Interrupt LS signal for 1 µs, 1 ms, 100 ms; restore; measure recovery.
cases.stimulus: IDLE + read commands with injected slips.
cases.expected: Alignment achieved on every phase; recovered after each slip; no false command execution.
cases.pass_criteria: 100 % alignment; recovery within implementation limit (to be declared) with no spurious write executed.
cases.fail_criteria: Stuck misaligned; spurious command; permanent lock loss.

LS triggers allow a fixed trigger latency of 3.4 µs with ±4 ns accuracy via the delay value. ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Introductory text; §8.3.2.1 makes delay usage quality-of-implementation.

cases.objective: Characterise latency and jitter between Host trigger event and Device exposure start for LS triggers.
cases.preconditions: Host with trigger input; Device strobe output.
equipment: Reference CXP frame grabber (Host) with GenTL producer
Pulse/function generator (trigger source)
Sampling oscilloscope (≥ 4× bit rate BW) with eye/jitter analysis, 75→50 Ω adapter
Logic analyzer / probe on DUT trigger-exposure-strobe output
procedure: Apply 10⁴ trigger edges asynchronous to the LS character clock.
Measure event → Device strobe latency.
Compute mean and peak-to-peak jitter; compare to declared quality-of-implementation (informative §4.7: 3.4 µs, ±4 ns).
cases.expected: Fixed latency; jitter ≪ one LS character (480 ns) if delay value used.
cases.pass_criteria: Within DUT declaration (NOT PROVIDED); informative comparison to §4.7.
cases.fail_criteria: Jitter ≈ 480 ns p-p (delay ignored) where compensation is claimed.

emulator.scope: The trigger event and the device's strobe are time stamps of the bench (the sim time of the Table 15 leader's first bit, UPLINK_MARK, and of the recreated trigger, TRIG_OUT), so the plan's 10^4 edges shrink to 40 and the §4.7 figures (3.4 us, +-4 ns) are not the device's declaration (none given): the bench's own bit rate and rx_clk apply. Needs the device's test bench (character link, TRIG_OUT and bench times); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Bench reset, inputs 0; one falling trigger puts the recreated trigger low.
40 times: a rising trigger with a random Delay 0..239 at a random character position of an IDLE word, then a falling one.
For each rising trigger: event = leader's first bit - (239 - Delay) x bit / 24 (§8.3.2.1, Figure 20); latency = recreated rising edge - event; also the edge - leader time without the Delay.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every rising trigger recreated once; the compensated latency varies by no more than 10 ns (one rx_clk, the device's stated resolution) + 1 ns (the bench's time grain); the uncompensated times spread far wider (the Delay is used). Mean latency reported.
emulator.fail_criteria: A trigger not recreated, a latency jitter above the limit, or a spread that shows the Delay ignored.

equipment: FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
procedure: Send rising trigger; then ConnectionReset.
Check internal trigger state = de-asserted.
cases.pass_criteria: Pass.

emulator.scope: The device's trigger signal is seen as the bench's TRIG_OUT: a level, or a strobe of the edge the device passes (cfg_trig_polarity 0: rising, 1: falling). With a strobe the de-assertion is visible only as the falling-edge effect under polarity 1. Link settings are restored afterwards. Needs the device's test bench (character link, TRIG_OUT, TRIG_IN and TRIG_POLARITY); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Bench reset (power-up), inputs 0: no recreated trigger.
Polarity 0: one falling trigger, a rising trigger (the reading: level or strobe), ConnectionReset, then a rising trigger.
Strobe devices, polarity 1 (trigger input held at its de-asserted level): a falling trigger, a rising trigger, ConnectionReset.
Device -> Host: the trigger input asserted (K28.4, acknowledged), ConnectionReset, the packets after it recorded; input low, then high again.

emulator.fail_criteria: A recreated trigger at power-up, a trigger left asserted (a level that stays high, no falling-edge effect under polarity 1), a rising trigger after the reset not recreated, or the device trigger dead after the reset.

cases.title: Device→Host HS trigger format and ack rules

requirements.text: Device-sent HS trigger: 4×K28.4 rising / 4×K28.2 falling, then 4×delay (3 − whole characters elapsed; 0 if unused), inserted at the next word boundary.
After sending a trigger the Device shall not send a new trigger until acknowledged, unless the transmission timeout has elapsed (then resend or send new).
A Device register should control the Device→Host trigger ack timeout (default set by Device, Host-overridable).

cases.objective: Verify Table 16 format, word-boundary insertion, no new trigger before ack, timeout behaviour.
equipment: FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator/Questa with Host BFM, scoreboards
CXP protocol exerciser / Host emulator (character-level upconnection generation, error injection)
CXP protocol analyzer (passive tap, 8B/10B character capture, timestamps)
procedure: Generate Device events at random phases; decode 4×K28.4/4×K28.2 + 4×delay; check delay = 3 − whole chars (or 0).
Hold off Host acks: verify no new trigger until timeout; then resend/new.
Change timeout register (if present).

emulator.scope: Device events are edges of the bench trigger input (TRIG_IN) while the device streams its test pattern; 20 instead of random phases without bound; the host acknowledges every trigger at once. The Delay is judged against its range only (the bench does not time the input's edge within a character). The timeout register §8.3.3 recommends is recorded, not required. Times are the bench's (the device's milliseconds, from the time stamps of the packets on both links), not the host's wall clock. Needs the device's test bench (TRIG_IN, the character link and bench times); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Reset the device through the bench with the input de-asserted; select the test pattern and stream.
After the first image header, 20 times: wait a random 5 and 40 ms, toggle the input (bench time taken), wait for the trigger packet, acknowledge it (Table 17).
Stop; judge the triggers, their bench times against the input's changes and the host's acknowledgments, and the stream.
emulator.pass_criteria: One trigger packet per edge, alternating 4 x K28.4 / 4 x K28.2, each clean with Delay 0..3; each whose predecessor's acknowledgment had reached the device (10000 ns after its last bit on the uplink) on the wire within 1000 ns of the input's change, inserted into the packet in progress when it met one (at least one did); none before the acknowledgment of the previous one reached the device (or 40960 ns, the device's timeout); the stream around them clean (Table 19, tags, framing).
emulator.fail_criteria: A missing, extra, malformed or wrong-kind packet; a trigger held back to a packet's end; a trigger before the previous one's acknowledgment or timeout; a damaged stream packet.

cases.title: Partial writes into the user window

requirements.text: On a valid command the Device shall execute it and transmit one final acknowledgment after execution.

Command payload decode: word 0 = Cmd (P0: 0x00 read, 0x01 write, 0xFF reset) + 24-bit Size B (P1..P3); word 1 = 32-bit address (incrementing); write data N = ceil(B/4) words with zero padding; CRC over words 0..N+1.
For ack codes other than 0x00 and 0x04 the Size, Data and CRC fields shall be omitted.

cases.objective: Writes whose Size is not a multiple of 4 into the user register window change exactly the bytes they carry (Table 21: Size is the number of bytes written; §10.3 byte-addressed space): the device drives the APB byte enables (PSTRB), so the pad bytes of the last word leave the slave's bytes as they were.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every write answered 0x01; every word read back holds the written bytes where the write reached and the sentinel's bytes elsewhere.
cases.fail_criteria: A byte past Size changed (zeroed by the pad), a written byte missing, or a write refused.

emulator.scope: The user window is the bench's APB slave behind REG_STALL (0 ms here); it honours PSTRB. Needs the device's test bench (REG_STALL); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: For each Size of 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7: write sentinels to every word the write touches; write Size bytes (0x11, 0x22, ...) at the first; read the words back.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every write answered 0x01; every word read back holds the written bytes where the write reached and the sentinel's bytes elsewhere.
emulator.fail_criteria: A byte past Size changed (zeroed by the pad), a written byte missing, or a write refused.

cases.title: Pipelined commands

requirements.text: On a valid command the Device shall execute it and transmit one final acknowledgment after execution.

Host shall not send a new command before the final ack, except after 200 ms timeout, expired wait time, or a control channel reset. ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Device behaviour when a Host violates this (overlapping command) is unspecified.

Command payload decode: word 0 = Cmd (P0: 0x00 read, 0x01 write, 0xFF reset) + 24-bit Size B (P1..P3); word 1 = 32-bit address (incrementing); write data N = ceil(B/4) words with zero padding; CRC over words 0..N+1.
Ack format: 4×K27.7, 4×0x03, 4×code; for codes 0x00/0x04: Size word, N data words (zero padded), CRC over words 0..N+1; 4×K29.7.
Read ack Size shall equal the command Size B; padding bytes = 0.
Bootstrap and manufacturer register accesses up to and including 104 bytes shall be implemented as one Control Command message.

cases.objective: Commands sent back to back without waiting for the acknowledgments (§8.6.1.1 has the Host wait): every one answered in order with the right data while they do not overlap inside the Device; when they do, the Device keeps what its decision D7 says (the command executing and one waiting) and neither answers nor executes the rest.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every plain burst answered command for command, in order, with the right data, and the last write's value in place; behind the slow access exactly two final acknowledgments (the slow command's with its data, then the waiting one's), at most one Wait, no acknowledgment on the link later, MasterHostConnectionID holding the waiting write's value (the dropped writes not executed), the slow write landed, and the next read answered.
cases.fail_criteria: A lost, duplicated, reordered or wrong acknowledgment in a plain burst; behind the slow access a third final acknowledgment, a missing one, an acknowledgment after the burst, a dropped write that was executed, or no answer afterwards.

emulator.scope: A bootstrap access completes long before the next command has crossed the low-speed uplink, so real overlap needs a slow first command: a user-window access behind the bench's REG_STALL slave. Times are the bench's (the device's milliseconds, from the time stamps of the packets on both links), not the host's wall clock. Without REG_STALL only the plain bursts run.
procedure: Read registers with distinct values for the model; bursts of 2, 3, 4 and 8 reads of distinct registers sent back to back, idle; the same numbers of writes of MasterHostConnectionID; the read bursts again while the test pattern streams.

For a user-window slave of 50 and 150 ms: a user read followed at once by 2, 3, 4 and 8 minus 1 bootstrap reads, then a user write followed by writes of MasterHostConnectionID; wait the stall plus 100 ms; read MasterHostConnectionID and the user word back; a read of Standard.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every plain burst answered command for command, in order, with the right data, and the last write's value in place; behind the slow access exactly two final acknowledgments (the slow command's with its data, then the waiting one's), at most one Wait, no acknowledgment on the link later, MasterHostConnectionID holding the waiting write's value (the dropped writes not executed), the slow write landed, and the next read answered.

For the TYPE word (lanes P0+P1, P2+P3, P0+P3), the Cmd/Size word (P0+P1, P2+P3) and the address word (P0+P1, P2+P3): a damaged read and a damaged write, each followed by a read of Standard; wait 500 ms for an acknowledgment.
Writes of the sentinel with one TYPE character damaged, each lane.
SOP, 4 x 0x02, EOP; then a read of Standard.
Read MasterHostConnectionID.

With the slave at 20 ms: read the user word.

cases.pass_criteria: Every write answered 0x01; after at most one prior-limit packet in flight, packets are no longer than the value written (whole packet, bytes); each value carried packets; every packet matches Table 19 and the tags go on +1 mod 256 across the writes; the images are complete (2 per value).
cases.fail_criteria: A write refused, a packet after the one possible in-flight packet longer than the new value, a Table 19 defect, a tag break, an incomplete image or a stalled stream.

emulator.scope: A 256 x 64 test-pattern stream (the bench's generator when there is one). The plan's bounds are INIT-007 and BND-003 between acquisitions; this is the same register written without stopping. Registers the check changes are restored afterwards.
procedure: Set Width x Height to 256 x 64, StreamPacketSizeMax 4096 bytes; start the acquisition and wait for the first image header.
Without stopping, write StreamPacketSizeMax 256, 40 and 4096 in turn, each after 2 more image headers (at most 20000 ms each).
Stop; judge every packet against the last acknowledged value. A first packet after an acknowledgment may have started before it and may use the preceding limit.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every write answered 0x01; after at most one prior-limit packet in flight, packets are no longer than the value written (whole packet, bytes); each value carried packets; every packet matches Table 19 and the tags go on +1 mod 256 across the writes; the images are complete (2 per value).

cases.title: A trigger and a command with no gap

requirements.text: The receiver shall decode replicated P0..P3 characters with immunity to single bit errors.
Device shall decode LS trigger packets: K28.2 K28.4 K28.4 = rising, K28.4 K28.2 K28.2 = falling, followed by 3× delay; packet may start at any character boundary, including inside another packet.
Every received trigger packet shall be acknowledged with an I/O acknowledgment (4×K28.6, 4×0x01).
The I/O channel (triggers, I/O acks) is defined for the Master connection (connection 0) only.

cases.objective: Verify that a Table 15 trigger immediately before a command's SOP or immediately after its EOP (no IDLE between, §8.2.4: any character boundary) is taken as a trigger and the command as a command.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every write answered 0x01 and every read 0x00 with the value written; every trigger answered by one I/O acknowledgment and recreated once.
cases.fail_criteria: A command lost or spoiled by the trigger next to it, or a trigger not acknowledged or not recreated.

emulator.scope: Needs the device's test bench (character link and TRIG_OUT); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN. MasterHostConnectionID is restored afterwards.
procedure: Bench reset, inputs 0.

For each Delay of 0 and 239, trigger first and command first: one falling trigger, then in one character frame a rising trigger and a write of a fresh MasterHostConnectionID value; again with a read of it.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every write answered 0x01 and every read 0x00 with the value written; every trigger answered by one I/O acknowledgment and recreated once.
emulator.fail_criteria: A command lost or spoiled by the trigger next to it, or a trigger not acknowledged or not recreated.

cases.title: Triggers back to back

requirements.text: Every received trigger packet shall be acknowledged with an I/O acknowledgment (4×K28.6, 4×0x01).
Device shall decode LS trigger packets: K28.2 K28.4 K28.4 = rising, K28.4 K28.2 K28.2 = falling, followed by 3× delay; packet may start at any character boundary, including inside another packet.
The I/O channel (triggers, I/O acks) is defined for the Master connection (connection 0) only.
The delay value (239 − elapsed 2 ns units) may be used, at full or coarser resolution, to recreate the trigger with fixed latency (quality of implementation).

LS triggers allow a fixed trigger latency of 3.4 µs with ±4 ns accuracy via the delay value. ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Introductory text; §8.3.2.1 makes delay usage quality-of-implementation.

cases.objective: Verify that Table 15 triggers sent with no IDLE between them are each acknowledged and each recreated at its own event time (Figure 20): the tightest retrigger the low-speed link allows, since a packet lasts 60 bits and a Delay less than 10.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Three acknowledgments and two recreated rising edges per sequence; their spacing equals the leaders' spacing plus the Delay difference within 10 ns (one rx_clk) + 1 ns; the read answers.
cases.fail_criteria: A trigger not acknowledged or not recreated, a recreated edge moved by the neighbouring packet, or a link that no longer answers.

emulator.scope: Rising, falling and rising triggers in one character frame, no IDLE between them. With bench times the spacing of the two recreated rising edges is judged. Needs the device's test bench (character link and TRIG_OUT); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Bench reset, inputs 0.
For each Delay pair (first, third) of 0 and 239, 239 and 0 and 200 and 200: one falling trigger; then rising (first Delay), falling (Delay 120), rising (third Delay) back to back.
With bench times: the recreated rising edges' spacing against the leaders' spacing plus (third - first) x bit / 24.
A read.
emulator.pass_criteria: Three acknowledgments and two recreated rising edges per sequence; their spacing equals the leaders' spacing plus the Delay difference within 10 ns (one rx_clk) + 1 ns; the read answers.
emulator.fail_criteria: A trigger not acknowledged or not recreated, a recreated edge moved by the neighbouring packet, or a link that no longer answers.

cases.title: A resent trigger packet

requirements.text: Every received trigger packet shall be acknowledged with an I/O acknowledgment (4×K28.6, 4×0x01).
Device shall decode LS trigger packets: K28.2 K28.4 K28.4 = rising, K28.4 K28.2 K28.2 = falling, followed by 3× delay; packet may start at any character boundary, including inside another packet.
The I/O channel (triggers, I/O acks) is defined for the Master connection (connection 0) only.

cases.objective: Verify that a Table 15 trigger packet the Host resends (§8.3.3: allowed when the acknowledgment does not come within the timeout) is acknowledged again but recreates no second trigger event: the Host's trigger signal did not change.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every packet acknowledged (2 + 1 per step); one recreated rising edge per step.
cases.fail_criteria: A packet not acknowledged, or a resent packet recreated as a new trigger event.

emulator.scope: Needs the device's test bench (character link and TRIG_OUT); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Bench reset, inputs 0; one falling trigger.
A rising trigger and 2 copies of it back to back in one character frame.
One falling trigger; a rising trigger and 2 copies of it, each sent after the previous one was acknowledged.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every packet acknowledged (2 + 1 per step); one recreated rising edge per step.
emulator.fail_criteria: A packet not acknowledged, or a resent packet recreated as a new trigger event.

cases.title: Triggers on an extension connection

requirements.text: Every received trigger packet shall be acknowledged with an I/O acknowledgment (4×K28.6, 4×0x01).
Device shall decode LS trigger packets: K28.2 K28.4 K28.4 = rising, K28.4 K28.2 K28.2 = falling, followed by 3× delay; packet may start at any character boundary, including inside another packet.
The I/O channel (triggers, I/O acks) is defined for the Master connection (connection 0) only.

cases.objective: Verify that a Table 15 trigger arriving on an extension connection has no effect: §8.3 defines the I/O channel (triggers and I/O acknowledgments) for the Master connection (connection 0) only.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: No I/O acknowledgment and no recreated rising edge on the extension connection; back on the master connection the read answers and the rising trigger is acknowledged once and recreated once.
cases.fail_criteria: A trigger acknowledged or acted on over the extension connection, or the master connection not working after.

emulator.scope: The connection is made an extension one by the bench strap (EXT_LINK = 1, from_extension_link_i). Needs the device's test bench (character link, TRIG_OUT and EXT_LINK); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Bench reset, inputs 0; one falling trigger puts the recreated trigger low.
EXT_LINK = 1: 6 triggers, rising and falling alternately, Delays spread over 0..239.
EXT_LINK = 0: a read; one rising trigger.
emulator.pass_criteria: No I/O acknowledgment and no recreated rising edge on the extension connection; back on the master connection the read answers and the rising trigger is acknowledged once and recreated once.

cases.title: TestMode entered during a stream and an unacknowledged device trigger

requirements.text: The transmitter shall give priority to control data over test data.
When TestMode changes 1→0 the Device shall complete the test packet currently being transmitted.

In Test Mode the Device shall not transmit data other than connection test packets or control packets (plus IDLE). ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Unclear whether trigger packets / I/O acknowledgements (I/O channel) are allowed during Test Mode.
Every received trigger packet shall be acknowledged with an I/O acknowledgment (4×K28.6, 4×0x01).

cases.objective: Verify that TestMode entered while the Device streams and while its trigger waits for the Host's acknowledgment completes the stream packet on the wire, starts no new one, keeps the trigger and I/O channel working (D2) with no lost or stale packet, and that streaming resumes afterwards.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every connection-test packet intact; no stream packet between the first and the last test packet; every stream packet Table 19 (none torn) with tags +1 across TestMode; every image that starts after TestMode complete; the device's trigger packets R then F (a resend of an unacknowledged level allowed); one clean I/O acknowledgment per host trigger and no other.
cases.fail_criteria: A torn stream packet, a stream packet in TestMode, a tag restart, an incomplete image after TestMode, a lost, doubled or stale trigger or acknowledgment.

emulator.scope: Device events are edges of the bench trigger input; the stream is the test pattern. Needs the device's test bench (TRIG_IN and the character link); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Reset the device through the bench with the trigger input low; select the test pattern; record.
AcquisitionStart; after the first image header raise the trigger input and wait for its packet.
Without acknowledging it: TestMode = 1; after 20 ms acknowledge it; two host triggers (rising, falling); lower the trigger input and acknowledge its packet.
Hold 100 ms; TestMode = 0; wait for two more image headers; AcquisitionStop.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every connection-test packet intact; no stream packet between the first and the last test packet; every stream packet Table 19 (none torn) with tags +1 across TestMode; every image that starts after TestMode complete; the device's trigger packets R then F (a resend of an unacknowledged level allowed); one clean I/O acknowledgment per host trigger and no other.
emulator.fail_criteria: A torn stream packet, a stream packet in TestMode, a tag restart, an incomplete image after TestMode, a lost, doubled or stale trigger or acknowledgment.

cases.title: Withheld and late I/O acknowledgments, edge bursts

requirements.text: Device-sent HS trigger: 4×K28.4 rising / 4×K28.2 falling, then 4×delay (3 − whole characters elapsed; 0 if unused), inserted at the next word boundary.
After sending a trigger the Device shall not send a new trigger until acknowledged, unless the transmission timeout has elapsed (then resend or send new).
A Device register should control the Device→Host trigger ack timeout (default set by Device, Host-overridable).

equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every packet clean Table 16; after each burst the last packet (or none, when the input is back at the level the host holds) leaves the host at the input's level; each trigger starts no earlier than the end of the host's next acknowledgment on the uplink, or 40960 ns after the previous trigger.
cases.fail_criteria: A malformed packet, a host left at the wrong level, or a trigger before the acknowledgment or the timeout.

emulator.scope: Device events are edges of the bench trigger input; the device's transmission timeout is its design value (40960 ns on this bench). Times are the bench's (the device's milliseconds, from the time stamps of the packets on both links), not the host's wall clock. Needs the device's test bench (TRIG_IN, the character link and bench times); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Reset the device through the bench with the input de-asserted.
Host silent: bursts of 2, 4 and 8 edges, 8 us of the device's time apart (faster than a host acknowledgment's round trip and the timeout); wait 300 ms after each; bring the input back low.
Host acknowledging each trigger as soon as it sees it: the same bursts.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every packet clean Table 16; after each burst the last packet (or none, when the input is back at the level the host holds) leaves the host at the input's level; each trigger starts no earlier than the end of the host's next acknowledgment on the uplink, or 40960 ns after the previous trigger.
emulator.fail_criteria: A malformed packet, a host left at the wrong level, or a trigger before the acknowledgment or the timeout.

cases.title: Device trigger input polarity

requirements.text: Device-sent HS trigger: 4×K28.4 rising / 4×K28.2 falling, then 4×delay (3 − whole characters elapsed; 0 if unused), inserted at the next word boundary.
After sending a trigger the Device shall not send a new trigger until acknowledged, unless the transmission timeout has elapsed (then resend or send new).
A Device register should control the Device→Host trigger ack timeout (default set by Device, Host-overridable).

cases.objective: Verify that a device trigger packet carries the edge of the trigger signal (Table 16: K28.4 rising, K28.2 falling) whatever the sense of the trigger input: with an active-low input the pin's falling edge is the trigger's rising edge.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: For both polarities every assertion gives one 4 x K28.4 + 4 x Delay packet and every de-assertion one 4 x K28.2 packet, in order, each clean with Delay 0..3.

emulator.scope: The trigger input and its polarity strap are bench inputs (TRIG_IN, TRIG_POLARITY). Needs the device's test bench (TRIG_IN, TRIG_POLARITY and the character link); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: For polarity 0 (active high) and 1 (active low): reset the device through the bench with the input at its de-asserted level (or drive the pins without a bench reset); acknowledge what the start sent.
3 times: assert the input, wait for the trigger packet, acknowledge it (Table 17), wait 20 ms; de-assert it, the same.
emulator.pass_criteria: For both polarities every assertion gives one 4 x K28.4 + 4 x Delay packet and every de-assertion one 4 x K28.2 packet, in order, each clean with Delay 0..3.
emulator.fail_criteria: A missing, extra or wrong-kind packet (the pin level sent instead of the trigger's), or a malformed one.

cases.title: Uplink bit-rate tolerance

requirements.text: IDLE presence should be checked on each active connection; after a threshold of misses the receiver should be reset (re-align).
The receiver shall perform word alignment.

cases.objective: Verify that the Device's low-speed receiver takes a Host whose bit rate is off the Device's clock by up to the sum of the two ends' tolerances (§6.7: each +-100 ppm), and measure how far beyond that it still works.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Every read answered 0x00 with Standard at offsets up to +-200 ppm and back at 0 ppm; beyond, the first offset per sign that loses a read is recorded.
cases.fail_criteria: A lost or wrong read at +-200 ppm or less, or after the return to 0 ppm.

emulator.scope: The host's bit rate is offset through the bench (UPLINK_PPM); the Device's clock is exact, so the offset is the relative error of the two. Needs the device's test bench (UPLINK_PPM); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: For each offset in 100, 200, 1000, 5000 and 10000 ppm, positive and negative: set it, one read to settle, then 20 reads of Standard.
Back at 0 ppm: one read to settle, then 20 reads.
emulator.pass_criteria: Every read answered 0x00 with Standard at offsets up to +-200 ppm and back at 0 ppm; beyond, the first offset per sign that loses a read is recorded.
emulator.fail_criteria: A lost or wrong read at +-200 ppm or less, or after the return to 0 ppm.

cases.title: Test receiver: the last payload words and a K character in the body

requirements.text: Device Test Receiver: compare against local sequence, increment TestErrorCount[m] per differing word and TestPacketCountRx[m] per test packet received.
Host shall have R/W access to TestErrorCount[m] and TestPacketCountRx[m]; writing 0 resets the selected counter.
Device shall process received test packets at all times regardless of TestMode.

cases.objective: Verify that the Device's Test Receiver compares every one of the 1024 payload words of a Table 23 packet, the last two included, and that a K character inside the payload counts as one different word of a packet that still counts (§8.7.1, §8.7.2).
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: After each packet TestPacketCountRx is one more and TestErrorCount grows by the number of words that differ: the corrupted ones, and one for the word carrying the K28.5.
cases.fail_criteria: A corrupted word not counted (the last two in particular), a packet lost or counted twice, or an error counted for the clean packet.

emulator.scope: Host test packets as character streams (CXC1) with one IDLE word after each. Needs the device's test bench (character link); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Clear TestErrorCount and TestPacketCountRx.
For each set of payload words in 1022 and 1023, 1023 and 0 and 1023: one Table 23 packet with those words corrupted (one byte lane each); read both counters.
One packet with the data character in lane P0 of payload word 500 replaced by K28.5; read.
One clean packet; read.
emulator.pass_criteria: After each packet TestPacketCountRx is one more and TestErrorCount grows by the number of words that differ: the corrupted ones, and one for the word carrying the K28.5.
emulator.fail_criteria: A corrupted word not counted (the last two in particular), a packet lost or counted twice, or an error counted for the clean packet.

cases.title: Counter clear in the middle of a test-packet burst

requirements.text: TestErrorCountSelector shall hold a valid connection ID 0..n−1, or n for the HS upconnection. ⚑ NEEDS SPECIFICATION CLARIFICATION: Reaction to an out-of-range selector write is not specified.
Host shall have R/W access to TestErrorCount[m] and TestPacketCountRx[m]; writing 0 resets the selected counter.
TestPacketCountTx[m] counts transmitted test packets; host write 0 resets it.
Connection reset: TestMode = 0, TestErrorCountSelector = 0, all test counters = 0.
Device Test Receiver: compare against local sequence, increment TestErrorCount[m] per differing word and TestPacketCountRx[m] per test packet received.
Device shall process received test packets at all times regardless of TestMode.

cases.objective: Verify that writing 0 to TestErrorCount and TestPacketCountRx while host test packets are arriving clears exactly what came before the write and counts everything after it (§8.7.3, §10.3.37, §10.3.39).
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: Both writes answered 0x01; TestPacketCountRx equals the packets after the clear and TestErrorCount their corrupted words; the clean packets add to the packet counter only.
cases.fail_criteria: A write not answered 0x01, a counter that kept what came before the clear or lost what came after it, or a clear of one counter that moved the other.

emulator.scope: On one low-speed upconnection a command can only sit between two test packets, so the clear falls exactly between two of them: one character stream (CXC1) carries the burst with one IDLE word after every packet, the two clearing writes, and the rest of the burst. Needs the device's test bench (character link); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Clear the counters; send 12 Table 23 packets, each with 2 corrupted words, with writes of 0 to TestErrorCount and to TestPacketCountRx (8 bytes) between packet 5 and the next, as one character stream.
Read TestErrorCount and TestPacketCountRx once the burst is through.
Send 3 clean packets; read both again.
emulator.pass_criteria: Both writes answered 0x01; TestPacketCountRx equals the packets after the clear and TestErrorCount their corrupted words; the clean packets add to the packet counter only.
emulator.fail_criteria: A write not answered 0x01, a counter that kept what came before the clear or lost what came after it, or a clear of one counter that moved the other.

A rectangular line marker (4×K28.3, 4×0x02) shall be sent before each line.
Rectangular image: size known before sending; every line same length and horizontal offset; every pixel same type.
Xsize/Ysize = image width/height in pixels; Xoffs/Yoffs = offset relative to the full Device image.

Maximum-density packing for 8/10/12/14/16-bit pixels/components per Figures 27–31 (little-end-first packing starting at P0 bit 0).

cases.objective: Verify that a sensor frame whose framing breaks the pixel port's rules (SOF inside a frame, a short or long line, stray pixels, a missing or early EOF) does not corrupt stream packets or disturb the next frame; and that short well-formed frames sent back to back keep their own header metadata.

cases.fail_criteria: A packet that breaks Table 19, a good frame lost, altered or carrying another frame's metadata, a PacketTag break, or no answer.

For each kind of sof_mid_frame, short_line, long_line, stray_pixels, missing_eof, early_eof and metadata_back_to_back: send the malformed 16 x 4 frame (for metadata_back_to_back: 6 well-formed frames of 1..3 x 1..2 pixels back to back instead), then a well-formed frame with its own SourceTag; record the stream.

Maximum-density packing for 8/10/12/14/16-bit pixels/components per Figures 27–31 (little-end-first packing starting at P0 bit 0).
Master connection control channel shall provide full register access.
On a valid command the Device shall execute it and transmit one final acknowledgment after execution.

Bootstrap and manufacturer register accesses up to and including 104 bytes shall be implemented as one Control Command message.
Device Test Receiver: compare against local sequence, increment TestErrorCount[m] per differing word and TestPacketCountRx[m] per test packet received.

cases.objective: Verify that the stream, register access, host connection-test packets and host triggers, all at the same time, each stay correct: no stream packet or image damaged, no command lost or answered wrongly, every test packet counted without error, every trigger acknowledged and recreated.
equipment: Emulator host (src/emu/host) over the FIFO link
cases.pass_criteria: The stream scoreboard is clean with at least 2 complete images equal to the golden model; every command is answered as the model predicts; TestPacketCountRx equals the test packets sent with TestErrorCount 0; every trigger gets one Table 17 acknowledgment and the recreated trigger follows them.

emulator.scope: One host thread interleaves the traffic; the link queues it, so the device sees commands, test packets and triggers arrive while it streams. The register model covers MasterHostConnectionID (random values) and read-only registers (StreamPacketSizeMax and ConnectionConfig are left alone: they restart packets and tags). Needs the device's test bench (character link and TRIG_OUT); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN.
procedure: Reset the device through the bench; Mono8, TestPattern Bars, 64 x 32; clear the test counters; put the recreated trigger low.

Start the acquisition; once the first image header is in, run 6 rounds of: one host test packet, 4 random reads (model registers) or MasterHostConnectionID writes, 2 Table 15 triggers of random kind and Delay; then wait for 2 more images and stop.

Judge the stream (Table 19, tags, framing, pixels against the golden Bars model), every command against the model, TestPacketCountRx / TestErrorCount, the I/O acknowledgments and the recreated trigger.

cases.title: IDLE baseline

equipment: FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator (src/verif/)

cases.title: §8.2.4 insertion — a trigger inside a control command
cases.objective: §8.2.4: a trigger indication may be inserted between two words of a long packet, and both survive — the trigger fires and is I/O-acked, the command still executes and is acknowledged 0x00. The host sends a control read and, three word times in, inserts a Table 15 trigger (six characters, at a character boundary), as a compliant host does.
equipment: FPGA/RTL testbench: cocotb + pyuvm on Verilator (src/verif/)

emulator.scope: §8.2.4: a rising trigger inserted 12 characters into a read of MasterHostConnectionID; both must survive. Host triggers go up as Table 15 low-speed triggers (6 characters, CXC1 frames), the form the spec gives the low-speed uplink. Needs the device's test bench (character link and TRIG_OUT); a device without it shows the case NOT RUN. As in UVM (cfg_run = 0 unless a test turns the generator on), the bench stops a free-running test-pattern generator for the test.
procedure: Send a falling trigger so the recreated trigger starts low.
Send the read with a Table 15 rising trigger after its first 12 characters, as one CXC1 frame.
Collect the command's acknowledgment, the I/O acknowledgment and the TRIG_OUT edges.
emulator.pass_criteria: The read answers 0x00 with the register's value; the trigger is acknowledged once and raises the recreated trigger once (a level, or one strobe).
emulator.fail_criteria: The command lost, NACKed or answered wrongly, or the trigger not acknowledged or not recreated.
